text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'eu-dedicated-4' — queue latency >500ms, GPU util 93%, queue depth rising. alert: https://alerts.redwood/alert/8123

alex: oncall ack, I'm taking this. pinging infra and platform.

priya: looking at dashboards — autoscaler hasn't added replicas in last 10m. pool config shows `burst_enabled: false` and `min_replicas: 2`.

jason: if burst is off the reserved burst capacity path won't be used. recommend: 1) enable burst, 2) bump min_replicas to 4, 3) apply emergency org-level rate cap to top consumer.

sana: +1. Top org is `acme-inc` ~65% of tokens for this pool. If we throttle them temporarily we should see queue drop quickly.

emily-cs: are customers impacted? which ones? need to message CS if we throttle.

priya: acme-inc is Dedicated customer on this pool. they may see slower responses or timeouts until we scale. I'll perform the config changes and add a temporary rate limit.

priya: executing mitigation steps now:
```bash
# enable burst capacity on pool
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.internal/pools/eu-dedicated-4 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"burst_enabled":true}'

# bump min replicas
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.internal/pools/eu-dedicated-4 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"min_replicas":4}'

# apply org-level emergency rate limit (60 rps)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/quotas -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"org_id":"acme-inc","pool":"eu-dedicated-4","rps":60,"ttl_sec":3600}'
```

deploy-bot: config change accepted — burst_enabled=true applied to eu-dedicated-4 at 2026-05-02T15:12:10Z.

infra-bot: autoscaler triggered: scaling replicas 2 -> 6 for eu-dedicated-4 (reason: queue_latency>400ms).

priya: seeing queue drain — 90th pct latency down to 180ms within 90s. throughput slightly throttled for acme-inc.

emily-cs: I'll ping Acme CS with a short note: "Transient performance incident on eu-dedicated-4; we've enabled burst capacity and applied a 1hr emergency throttle to reduce impact. Monitoring closely." want me to send now?

alex: yes please. add that we'll revert throttle once queue stable for 15m. :thumbsup:

jason: handing off monitoring to me for the next shift. checklist: watch queue depth, GPU util, confirm autoscaler stabilizes, and schedule rollback of rate cap after 1h if healthy. @alex I'm good to take over now.

alex: lgtm. leaving pager to @jason. noted steps to revert:
```bash
# remove org quota
curl -X DELETE https://api.redwood.internal/quotas/acme-inc/eu-dedicated-4 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

# if stable, set min_replicas back to 2
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.internal/pools/eu-dedicated-4 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"min_replicas":2}'
```

jason: monitoring — current metrics: GPU util 68%, queue depth falling, p95 latency 240ms. I'll keep an eye for 1hr and then revert throttle if steady. opening incident thread for postmortem.

priya: quick note: autoscaler didn't fire earlier because our burst-disabled health gate prevented using burst slots during steady ramp. we'll capture root cause and propose a default config change for pools with high-volume dedicated customers.

emily-cs: Acme CS notified. they acknowledged and appreciate proactive throttle to preserve overall stability.

jason: thanks team. will follow up with a short post-incident summary and action items. :white_check_mark:
